meta.title: Competitor Radar
meta.niche: AI-powered automated investing and personal wealth management apps

analysis.summary: Wealthfront and M1 Finance are the only active publishers. Wealthfront teaches savers, while M1 refreshes product pages and starts an AI wealth push. Clera has no pages in the data.

points.text: Wealthfront added 5 new pages and updated 6, mostly plain-English money guides, so it is building trust with learners before selling.
M1 Finance updated 13 older pages, 11 of them product pages, which looks like a refresh push aimed at people ready to open accounts.
M1 Finance published 'AI Wealth Management' and 'M1 Advisor' pages, so it is moving first on the AI advisor story Clera would want to own.

Wealthfront.play: Teaches savings, 529s and mortgage rates, and announces new products like its Brokerage Account and 2026 launches.

Betterment.play: Very large site, but only one new page: a Solo 401(k) vs SEP IRA comparison.

M1 Finance.play: Refreshes account and borrowing pages, and launches AI wealth management and M1 Advisor content.

Public.com.play: Has 519 pages but published or updated nothing in the last 30 days.

Titan.play: No pages found in the data, so no content play is visible.

shared.title: Rate and account-feature selling
shared.text: Wealthfront promotes a 3.55% cash account APY and M1 promotes a 3.35% APY plus 4.24% borrowing. Both lead with numbers, so Clera needs a clear value hook.

shared.title: Account-choice guidance
shared.text: Wealthfront's 'Which account should I open?' and M1's many account-type pages both help people pick a product. Clera can do the same for AI investing.

gaps.title: Honest AI explainer
gaps.text: Only M1 has AI wealth pages, and Wealthfront has one page about what LLMs get wrong. Clera could own plain-English answers on how AI investing works and where it fails.

gaps.title: AI vs human advisor comparisons
gaps.text: Nobody publishes a direct comparison of AI advice with human advisors or robo-advisors (automated investing services). Comparing shoppers need this, and Clera could write it first.

gaps.title: Regular content engine
gaps.text: Betterment, Public.com and Titan show little or no recent publishing. A steady stream of guides on AI investing questions faces little competition from them.
